headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Roo Code can write/egress while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP server/API/webhook surfaces, and Roo Code can use MCP plus read/write the VS Code workspace. That creates a default bridge where attacker-controlled content from OpenMetadata can be fed into Roo Code’s tool-use context and interpreted as instructions. The pairwise pathway is documented by both profiles; uncertainty is about exact parser behavior, so severity stays high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is surfaced through MCP, APIs, or webhooks into Roo Code prompts or tool context, injection is possible.
IF Roo Code processes workspace or MCP content as trusted instructions without provenance checks, attacker text can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata outputs into Roo Code prompts.
Add provenance tags and instruction/content separation in the MCP bridge.
Restrict Roo Code to read-only mode for OpenMetadata-derived content.
Review and sanitize webhook payloads before they reach the workspace.
requires-engineering: add parser-level allowlists for tool commands.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/trust data, while Roo Code reads workspace files and can egress broadly to configured model APIs. If both share a workspace or MCP channel, sensitive metadata can flow from OpenMetadata into Roo Code and then to a third-party backend. The leakage path exists in default setups, but the blast radius is bounded by the workspace and configured APIs.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata exports sensitive catalog or governance records into a shared workspace, Roo Code can read them.
IF Roo Code is configured with a remote model API, workspace contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep OpenMetadata and Roo Code in separate workspaces.
Disable or minimize remote model API use for sensitive projects.
Redact governance and lineage fields before passing files to Roo Code.
Use a local-only model endpoint for the pair.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on MCP/file transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata can run multiple instances and uses APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP; Roo Code has broad filesystem write, git modification, shell, and network egress, with shared state via filesystem. Both can mutate the same workspace or adjacent project state, so concurrent edits and git conflicts are plausible by default. Because no locking is documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites files while OpenMetadata emits updates into the same tree, state corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Serialize write access with a simple lock file.
Pause one agent before the other edits git state.
Limit Roo Code to read-only when OpenMetadata is syncing.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata produces governance, lineage, and trust metadata that Roo Code can ingest through files or MCP and then act on with shell/git/network privileges. If Roo Code treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad catalog entry or stale lineage record can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. The pairwise action chain is directly supported by both profiles, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses OpenMetadata outputs as facts without verification, downstream edits can be wrong.
IF Roo Code is allowed to commit or run shell actions based on catalog metadata, errors can propagate into persistent changes.
mitigations: Require human review before Roo Code acts on OpenMetadata-derived facts.
Add a verification step against source systems before edits.
Restrict Roo Code from auto-committing changes.
Mark OpenMetadata outputs as advisory, not authoritative.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly handles governance and lineage data, while Roo Code handles source code and model-provider API keys and can send context to configured external APIs. The profiles do not document residency or certification mismatches, so I cannot claim a specific breach; however, the pair creates a plausible compliance gap around retention and third-party transmission of governed metadata. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF governed metadata or regulated code is routed through Roo Code to a remote model API, retention and residency obligations may be implicated.
IF OpenMetadata records are retained differently from Roo Code workspace artifacts, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets out of Roo Code workspaces.
Use a local model endpoint for compliance-sensitive tasks.
Review retention settings for both tools before shared use.
Separate secrets from catalog exports.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls.
